ecus.name: HV battery cell monitoring unit (slave / CSC / BMU-slave boards)
ecus.function: Per-module cell voltage and temperature measurement, passive balancing, isolated daisy-chain (or wireless) link to the master.

pcb.layers: not published in any source found for a production CMU; 4 layers (engineering judgement)
pcb.size: not published in any source found for a production CMU. Reference: ST AEK-POW-BMS63EN (one L9963E node, 4-14 cells) is 100 x 76 mm (evaluation board, not production).
pcb.technology: Rigid FR4 AFE board; the cell sense lines increasingly run on an FPC cell-contacting system (CCS) welded to the busbars instead of a wire harness. BYD Blade CMUs are laser-welded to the cell output poles.
pcb.laminate: FR4 (engineering judgement); grade not published in any source found
pcb.boards: BYD Blade pack: 11 CMUs of two types, each with 22 sampling points (AFE + daisy-chain chips; balancing presence reported inconsistently). NXP HVBMS reference: one CMU board carries 4 cell controllers for up to 56 cells. VW ID.3 (Huber) slaves: 20% (Slave 4) and 50% (Slave 1) of board area is processing; Xpeng G6 (PSA ITC) uses one board design for Slave 3 and Slave 4.

ecus.name: HV battery management unit (master / BCU) + battery junction box (BJB / BDU) electronics
ecus.function: Pack state estimation and safety master; contactor and pyro-fuse control, pack voltage / current / insulation measurement in the BJB, vehicle CAN.

pcb.layers: not published in any source found; 4-6 layers (engineering judgement)
pcb.size: BCU board area 285 cm^2 (PSA ITC, Xpeng G6) and 270 cm^2 (Huber, VW ID.3).
pcb.technology: FR4 (engineering judgement); the BJB measurement board sits in the HV domain next to contactors / pre-charge (IVT-type sensors are placed in the PDU / BJB / HV box).
pcb.laminate: not published in any source found
pcb.boards: Master BCU + BJB/BDU electronics. BYD Blade: BMU has no separate shell, embedded in the BDU; BDU holds two main contactors, a BYD-made shunt current sensor and a 400 A fuse. NXP HVBMS reference: separate BMU (RD-K344BMU) and BJB (RD772BJBTPLEVB) boards. PHEVs commonly centralized (one board), BEVs master-slave.

boardCostEvidence.claim: Huber Automotive's VW ID.3 BMS Slave 4 is about 20% more expensive than PSA ITC's Xpeng G6 Slave 4 (Yole teardown; absolute figures paywalled).

notes: No public absolute cost / ASP for a CMU, BMU, BJB board, 48 V BMS or IBS was found. NXP's RD-HVBMSCTBUN kit is listed by distributors at $2,699 - an evaluation-kit price, not a board cost, so it is not given as evidence.
Production CMU chip identity found only for BYD Blade (MAX17853). VW ID.3 / Xpeng G6 slave ICs, Tesla Model 3 BMB and the CATL Zeekr 001 CSC were searched without a named IC.
NXP claims the MC33777 cuts BJB monitoring component count by up to 80% (vendor claim): https://nxp.com/products/MC33777
ADI says its wBMS (GM Ultium) removes up to 90% of the pack wiring and up to 15% of pack volume (vendor claim): https://chargedevs.com/newswire/gm-to-debut-wireless-ev-battery-management-system/

Already priced in the catalogue (distributor, with observations) - not re-researched: BQ79616PAPRQ1, BQ79612PAPRQ1, BQ79656PAPRQ1, BQ79718BQPAPRQ1, BQ79600PWRQ1, MC33771CTA1AE, MC33772CTA1AE, MC33775ATA1AER2, MC33664ATL1EGR2, MC33665ATS4AE, ADBMS6830BCSWZ, ADBMS6815WCSWZ, ADBMS1818ASWAZ, ADBMS2950WFSCCSZ, LTC6813HLWE-1, LTC6811HG-1, LTC6820HMS, MAX17853, MAX17841B, L9963E-TR, L9963T-TR, TLE9012DQUXUMA1, TLE9015DQUXUMA1, TLE4972AE35D5XUMA1, MLX91220, ACS37002, TMCS1123, AMC1301, AMC1302, AMC3301, AMC3330, ISO1042, ISO7741, SN6501-Q1, SN6505B-Q1, UCC14240-Q1, DRV3946-Q1, S32K344, S32K358, TC375 / TC377 / TC387 / TC397, SAK-TC234LP-32F200F AC, FS26 (MFS2633), FS6500, TLF35584, TJA1145A, MPC5744P.
